<!--
Read CONTRIBUTING.md before opening a pull request. Review time is limited.
Meeting it makes a pull request eligible for review. Solve one underlying problem.
The same requirements apply to a draft.
The title is a Conventional Commit in plain language, such as
"fix(workspaces): an empty workspace keeps its name".
-->

## Problem

<!-- The problem in a sentence or two. Include what you expected, what you ran,
and the environment where that matters. -->

## Change

<!-- How this fixes that problem. When the diff spans projects, say why each
part is the same fix. An independent fix belongs in its own pull request. -->

## Scope and approval

<!-- Link the maintainer comment that approves the direction and the scope, or
the triaged bug issue. A link to the issue alone is not approval of a feature
or a behavior change.

For a very small fix of an obvious bug, say why it qualifies with no prior issue.
For an option on a behavior Winland already has, name that behavior, what the
option controls, and why the effect stays inside it. A new workflow, a new
default, or a wider behavior change still needs approval.

There is no line-count or file-count cutoff.

Fixes # -->

## Verification

<!-- The focused tests or manual checks, and what you observed. Say what you
could not check. "Tests pass" is not enough. A repo-wide run is not required.

A change someone can see needs before-and-after screenshots. Motion, timing,
or a gesture needs a short recording. Upload them here. Do not commit them. -->

<!-- An agent ends with the model and harness that did the work. -->
